full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin, J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated May 20, 2003 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1143 of 2001 quashing the proceedings of Special Case No.1 of 1996 of the Court of Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj. 

 3. The learned Sessions Judge sent the petition of complaint to the District Anti-Corruption Bureau (the Bureau) to hold investigation into the allegations and the Bureau after inquiry into the allegations in the petition of complaint lodged an FIR and on completion of investigation submitted charge-sheet against the Respondent No.1 under Section 409 read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. In due course the case records were sent to the Court of Special Judge, Sunamganj and thereupon Special Case No.1 of 1996 was registered and the Court took cognizance under Section 409 of the Penal Code and under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. Thereupon the Respondent No.1 moved the High Court Division seeking quashing of the proceedings of the aforesaid Special Case and obtained the Rule. 

 4. It was the contention of the Respondent No.1 that the allegations made in the FIR registered on the basis of the complaint filed before the Court of Sessions Judge as well as the facts stated in the charge-sheet do not disclose any case under section 409 of the Penal Code and Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947, that in the FIR as well as in the charge-sheet there is no material to constitute an offence of misappropriation of the fund of any authority or property of any organization, that continuation of the proceeding in the background of the materials on record is an abuse of the process of the Court and also harassing. 

 7. It may be mentioned in the auction held for selling the old office house the petitioner herein participated and his bid was Tk.27,100/- and as against that the highest bid was made at Tk.52,100/- by one Iron Miah. Bid money upon accepting which the old office house so sold was deposited in the government fund and this fact is not disputed by the petitioner herein. In the state of the aforesaid matter the High Court Division held "in view of this admitted fact it can not but be said that no case stand against the accused petitioner and continuation of the prosecution would amounts to harassment and abuse of the process of the Court". The High Court Division also held that facts or in other words allegations made in the FIR and the fact reflected in the charge-sheet do not constitute offence under Section 409 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. On the aforesaid finding the High Court Division quashed the proceedings of the special case.
